history: From Hugo Ensslin’s 1916 Recipes for Mixed Drinks, originally in equal parts. Modern specs pull the Chartreuse back so the whiskey survives.
whyItWorks: Chartreuse’s 130 herbs would flatten most whiskeys; Irish is soft and grassy enough to meet it rather than fight it.
steps: Stir all three with ice until well chilled.
Express an orange twist and drop it in.
techniqueNotes: The original 1:1:1 is a Chartreuse drink with whiskey in it. Start here and move toward equal parts if the room wants it.

substitutions.notes: Yellow is gentler and sweeter—use ¾ oz.
Bourbon works but the sweetness stacks; pull the vermouth to ½ oz.

name: Tipperary
description: Irish whiskey, sweet vermouth and green Chartreuse—an Irish Manhattan with a herbal streak.
